Documentation / Developer / Scene alignment

Scene alignment

PR1 supplies scene alignment only. Layout multi-selection/alignment and universal distribution remain deferred. Existing fixture distribution is unchanged.

Ownership and command publication

alignment_geometry accepts immutable projected rectangles and implements the six anchors once. A future Layout adapter can supply document rectangles directly. scene_alignment resolves typed chronological scene identities with BuildInteractiveTransformTargets and the existing interactive promotion policy, collects physical bounds, and passes world-axis translations to ExecuteBatch. The batch validates a complete candidate scene, preserves transform bases and hierarchy, and publishes through MutationTransaction exactly once. A no-op publishes nothing. Failed validation/loading/publication leaves scene and selection unchanged. Capture and execution run synchronously on the GUI event thread, so there is no event yield between geometry capture and commit. Other frontends must serialize scene mutation on their execution thread too.

The GUI owns controls, localized messages, diagnostics and normal scene/selection refresh. It performs no bounds or alignment arithmetic. The toolbar remains accessible in both scene workspaces; actions are disabled in Layout mode. Enablement resolves identities only and never loads geometry. Publication uses the established scene refresh boundary; incremental renderer notifications remain owned there.

Selection chronology

SelectionState adds OrderedSceneSelection, a runtime vector of typed UUIDs; vector position is the selection sequence. Category setters reconcile membership: surviving identities never move, removal deletes the identity, and a later addition appends it. Thus sorted table/viewer refreshes do not replace chronology. A batch of new identities in one setter uses ascending UUID order. Calls replacing several categories use their explicit call order (the existing shared adapters call fixture, truss, support, scene object, group). This policy makes no claim to individual click chronology within a rectangle/range selection. Explicit neutral replacement through OrderedSceneSelection::Replace honors caller order, removes duplicates, and does not reconstruct history from maps. No metadata, dirty state or Undo entry is added for chronology. Existing Undo snapshots retain order so history restoration does not change first/last reference identity. Shared command publication uses atomic SetSceneSelection membership synchronization to avoid clearing/re-adding groups. Project replacement clears the selection through existing Reset/load paths; the ordered-query boundary prunes deleted UUIDs before use.

Normalization preserves the earliest chronological occurrence of each surviving effective target. A group selected with a descendant or several leaves promoted to one group produces one target. Suppressed descendants inherit their surviving group identity using the same interactive target resolver. Missing identities or unresolved promotion abort with deterministic diagnostics. Reference selection happens after normalization, so first/last references stay fixed. Explicit group identities are accepted by the neutral adapter; existing GUI group highlighting/promotion continues to select groups through their members.

Bounds and resource ownership

SceneBounds is a CPU provider independent of renderer initialization. It reuses GeometryBoundsResolver for 3DS/GLB, the existing cached GDTF geometry tree for fixtures and GDTF-backed trusses/supports, and the shared renderer resource path resolver for scene/library resolution. No new resource manager is introduced. GDTF mesh coordinates are millimeters and node translations are meters; the provider converts translations once before measuring local fixture bounds. Immutable fixture bounds have a bounded 128-entry derived cache keyed by resource identity, mode, file size and modification time. The loader retains canonical archive ownership, content validation and extraction leases. Mesh cache invalidation remains in the existing resolver. World projection transforms all eight local AABB corners using the full matrix. SceneObject and Support geometry-instance matrices are composed with the node world matrix. Group bounds union descendants' world bounds; cycles, missing children and multiply owned geometry abort instead of double counting.

Only actual loaded meshes or authored GDTF primitives with complete positive dimensions qualify. GDTF dimension-box fallbacks are explicitly marked nonphysical without changing rendering behavior. Missing resources, absent/empty geometry and non-finite values fail the operation; there is no implicit insertion-point or invented-size fallback. AABB projection is conservative for irregular geometry. Dummy supports without physical resources cannot use geometric alignment. Insertion-point alignment is not exposed by this PR; it would require a separately named explicit policy.

Work planes

All calculation uses scene millimeters, independent of UI units and zoom. The visible selector is authoritative and defaults safely to XY, including in perspective. It never follows camera yaw. Choose XY for Top, XZ for Front, YZ for Side; changing viewport orientation does not silently override the selector.

Plane Screen horizontal Screen vertical Unchanged axis
XY +X +Y Z
XZ +X +Z Y
YZ -Y +Z X

Left/right refer to projected visual edges, including mirrored Side Y. Top uses maximum projected vertical extent. Only one corresponding world translation component changes per operation; rotation, scale and the other two coordinates are preserved. Extents and all deltas use one original immutable bounds snapshot.

Validation

SceneAlignment exercises the pure calculations, mixed chronology, policy normalization, repeated no-ops and transactional publication failure without GL. SceneAlignmentPhysicalBounds uses production CPU loaders, a real primitive GDTF archive and a bundled 3DS, including rotated fixtures/trusses, instance transforms, nested groups, missing resources, invalid transforms and dimension-box rejection. The existing batch, grouping and MVR interchange regressions remain relevant. SceneAlignmentBoundary guards the GUI-independent geometry/command boundary. These CTest tests run through the existing platform CI matrix.
